problem: Reactive navigation policies (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, NavDP) map observations directly to actions and lack anticipatory reasoning, so they collide in clutter. Modular world-model approaches (NWM, NavigateDiff) decouple imagination from control, adding latency and compounding errors, and most methods support only a single goal type. Autoregressive World-Action Models from manipulation are too slow and error-prone under large egocentric viewpoint changes.
motivation: Safe navigation in cluttered scenes needs foresight about near-future geometry, but long visual rollouts are slow and accumulate errors. Trajectories also need to be kinematically smooth, which visual conditioning alone does not give. A single policy that handles Image-, Point- and No-Goal navigation without retraining would be more practical.
key_idea: Jointly denoise long-horizon actions and a very short-horizon latent visual foresight in one shared DiT (asymmetric world-action modeling), conditioned on goal-modulated visual memory fused with egocentric ego-motion history, with a unified goal alignment for three goal types.
insight: Foresight helps most when it is short and tightly coupled to action generation. Ablation: H_vis=1 gives 50.2 SR, and SR falls to 46.2, 39.6 and 30.4 for H_vis=4, 8 and 24. A fully shared DiT beats decoupled (45.9) and partially shared (47.5) variants. Latent prediction alone gives +3.6 SR (42.1 to 45.7). Motion history alone helps in ClutterScenes but hurts in InternScenes, and the two together give the best result (50.2). The goal-alignment ablation shows a visual-only query favors Image-Goal and a geometric-only query favors Point-Goal, while combining them gives a more balanced policy and the best No-Goal result.
method: Unified Goal Alignment: a modality-specific encoder E_phi (ViT from scratch for image goals, sinusoidal encoding for relative coordinates, masked zero-state for no goal) yields e_g. Linear heads produce a visual query g_V and a geometric query g_G, trained with a symmetric InfoNCE alignment loss.
Goal-Modulated Visual Memory: DINOv2 patch tokens over a k=8 frame window are re-weighted by sigmoid(g_V V^T/sqrt(D)) and updated residually as V + alpha*V.

Trajectory-Aware Motion History: executed poses are converted to egocentric relative (dx, dy, dtheta), encoded by a causal Transformer, and queried with g_G via cross-attention to get a kinematic token o_kin.
Condition Fusion: a Transformer decoder whose learnable queries are biased by o_kin cross-attends to the goal-modulated visual memory, producing the conditioning context C (64 tokens).

Asymmetric Action-Foresight Generation: a 16-layer shared DiT with flow matching jointly denoises H_act=24 action tokens and H_vis=1 latent frame (SD-VAE 16x16x4 latents) through shared self-attention, cross-attention to C, and adaLN-Zero.
Training and inference: loss is action velocity MSE + 0.25 * latent velocity MSE + 0.1 * InfoNCE. Inference uses 10 Euler steps, samples 16 candidate trajectories and executes the first.

setting.backbone: Shared DiT (16 layers, hidden dim 384) trained from scratch, with frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 and frozen SD-VAE
setting.training_data: VLN-N1 (InternData): more than 200K simulated trajectories, over 400 hours, built on Replica, MP3D, Gibson, 3D-FRONT, HSSD and HM3D. About 8x120 GPU hours.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB history (8 frames) plus ego-motion pose history; goal image or relative point or none (RGB-D on the real robot)
setting.action_space: predicted trajectory waypoints (24-step horizon), tracked by MPC
setting.simulator: IsaacSim (ClutterScenes, InternScenes) with Dingo, G1 and H2 robots
setting.privileged: none at test time (uses odometry-accumulated ego-motion history)

numbers_note: No standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark is used; results are on the authors' IsaacSim ClutterScenes and InternScenes benchmark, so canonical names do not apply. Real-world result is reported only as an average of 85% success over 4 scenes with 10 trials each, with per-scene numbers shown only in a figure.
results: WAM-Nav beats the strongest baseline NavDP in zero-shot IsaacSim evaluation on all three tasks: Image-Goal 50.2 vs 43.4 SR, Point-Goal 80.4 vs 77.8 SR, and No-Goal area 171.1 vs 167.2. It needs 0.26 s latency and 0.7 TFLOPs, versus NWM at 1.43 s and 8.3 TFLOPs. On a real Unitree G1 it reaches 85% average success across 4 indoor and outdoor scenes.
limitations: Limited camera height and field of view cause missed low or near-field obstacles and delayed avoidance.
The policy does not model robot embodiment, so camera-level avoidance can collide with the body.
A single-stream goal variant beats the unified one on its own task (Only g_V 55.6 Image-Goal SR; Only g_G 83.5 Point-Goal SR), so balance across tasks costs peak performance.
